pattern.top_pattern: FL acute hospital spend is concentrated in a few authorized provider and product combinations
pattern.what_is_impacting: FL Medicaid ACUTE HOSPITAL admissions across ABD Non Dual, TANF Standard, and CHIP Standard
pattern.pattern_details: FL acute hospital spend growth is concentrated in a small set of authorized products and hospitals, which creates a clear provider-mix story. ABD Non Dual shows both more admissions and higher paid per admit, with Tampa General standing out on unit cost, while TANF Standard is mainly a volume story across Tampa General, AdventHealth Orlando, and Lakeland. CHIP Standard adds a smaller but similar acute hospital increase at AdventHealth Orlando.
pattern.why_it_matters: Because the pressure is concentrated, provider-specific contract, pricing, and authorization actions are more likely to work than broad market-wide changes.
pattern.recommended_next_step: Run provider-level contract and authorization review for Tampa General, AdventHealth Orlando, and Lakeland across the affected FL acute hospital products, prioritizing Tampa General ABD Non Dual pricing and TANF Standard admission growth.
evidence_summary: FL ABD Non Dual acute hospital spend increased about +$21.1M with roughly +1,169 admissions and higher paid per admit.
Tampa General alone added about +$3.7M in FL ABD Non Dual acute hospital spend, with paid per admit up about $8K.
FL TANF Standard acute hospital spend increased about +$15.4M with roughly +2,263 admissions, while paid per admit declined, confirming a volume-led provider mix shift.
A smaller FL acute hospital increase remains in ABD Non Dual and CHIP Standard at AdventHealth Orlando and Lakeland, adding about +$940K combined.
